standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma for a finitely generated module over a ring with an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-NAK (canonical Stacks tag 00DV), invoked at proof lines 162-163
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the surjectivity of the two composites modulo I into genuine surjectivity of psi o phi and phi o psi as maps of R-modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: A surjective endomorphism of a finite module is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-fun (canonical Stacks tag 05G8), invoked at proof line 164
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the surjectivity obtained from Nakayama to invertibility of the two composites, which is what makes phi an isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: The lifting property of projective modules against a surjection of rings, applied to finite projective modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the projectivity of P and P' recorded in the statement at source lines 148-149, used at proof lines 159-161 and 168-170
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the lift psi : P' -> P of the composite P' -> P'/IP' -> P/IP and the lift phi : P -> P' of P -> P/IP -> P'/IP'; both are the objects the remainder of the proof operates on.

core_obligations: Part (1): given an R-module map phi : P -> P' between finite projective modules whose reduction modulo I is an isomorphism, construct a lift psi : P' -> P of the inverse of that reduction, using the projectivity of P' against the surjection P -> P/IP (proof lines 159-161).

Apply Nakayama's lemma to the finite modules P and P' to conclude that both composites psi o phi and phi o psi are surjective, then upgrade surjectivity of an endomorphism of a finite module to invertibility (proof lines 162-165); this is the only place where the radical hypothesis on I is used.
Deduce assertion (1) of the statement, namely that phi itself is an isomorphism (proof line 165).

Part (2): starting from an isomorphism P/IP = P'/IP', lift the composite P -> P/IP -> P'/IP' to an R-module map phi : P -> P' using the projectivity of P, and apply part (1) to conclude that P and P' are isomorphic (proof lines 168-170).
proof_roadmap: Proof of (1): choose a lift psi : P' -> P of the inverse of the reduction of phi, possible because P' is projective (proof lines 159-161).

Use Nakayama to show psi o phi and phi o psi are surjective, then use that a surjective endomorphism of a finite module is an isomorphism to conclude that both composites, and hence phi, are isomorphisms (proof lines 162-165).
Proof of (2): choose an isomorphism P/IP = P'/IP' and lift the composite P -> P/IP -> P'/IP' to phi : P -> P', possible because P is projective (proof lines 168-170).
Apply part (1) to that phi to conclude that P and P' are isomorphic (proof line 170).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the uniqueness companion of the lift lemma of the same section: for finite projective modules over a ring it asserts that an R-module map whose reduction modulo an ideal I contained in the Jacobson radical is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism, and that isomorphism classes are detected modulo I (statement lines 146-155). The proof has to build the comparison map by hand twice: first a lift psi of the inverse of the reduction of phi, using the projectivity of P' against the surjection P -> P/IP (proof lines 159-161), then a lift phi of the composite P -> P/IP -> P'/IP', using the projectivity of P (proof lines 168-170). The decisive step is that Nakayama plus surjectivity of an endomorphism of a finite module converts surjectivity modulo I into invertibility of both composites, and it is applied twice with the roles of P and P' interchanged (proof lines 162-165). Both parts of the two-part statement live inside the counted span, and the only inputs are the two cited Algebra lemmas.
